title: State and Binding: one source of truth

videos.script: A screen shows one fact in several places. The planner's course screen ticks the sessions that are done, and adds them up at the bottom. {{truth}} The fact must live in one place. SwiftUI calls that place the source of truth. {{state}} A view that owns a value marks it with State. SwiftUI keeps it outside the view, and draws the view again when it changes. {{binding}} A view that changes somebody else's value is handed a binding. Read it, write it, and the write lands with the owner. {{byhand}} Then you build a binding yourself, in plain Swift, on your own machine. Two closures, one key path, and three lines of output that show the difference between a copy and a binding. {{stale}} Then a test that fails on purpose. A total stored beside the plan says ninety, and the plan says one hundred and fifty. {{traps}} Three ways state goes wrong, each with its cure. {{screens}} And the planner's first two screens, with one plan between them and no line that copies a number.
